Report_ID: All-cause mortality (death; one death after myocardial infarction)
Title: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of canakinumab in patients with peripheral artery disease
Author: Russell KS, Yates DP, Kramer CM, et al.
Comment: Mortality was not a prespecified endpoint; deaths reported only narratively as a reason for discontinuation. No deaths were described in the placebo group, so zero events were assumed for that arm (0/20). No effect estimate, CI, or p-value reported by the authors; RR not estimable without continuity correction. Denominators are the randomised/safety-analysis-set Ns (18 and 20).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Canakinumab 150 mg/1 mL sc monthly (on top of statin + antiplatelet)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Topic of Content: Interleukin-1β blockade (canakinumab) in peripheral artery disease
Participant type: Outpatients aged 18-85 with symptomatic peripheral artery disease and intermittent claudication confirmed by ankle-brachial index, on stable statin and antiplatelet therapy
Recruitment source: 16 clinical centers (United States n = 8, Germany n = 7, Jordan n = 1), 129 screened
Outcome measurement: Number of deaths reported per randomised group in the Results 'Patient characteristics' narrative
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality (death; one death after myocardial infarction)
effect_direction: unfavourable (1/18 deaths with canakinumab vs 0/20 with placebo)

Report_ID: All-cause mortality (death from any cause) at 24 weeks
Title: Interleukin-1 Blockade in Recently Decompensated Systolic Heart Failure: Results From REDHART (Recently Decompensated Heart Failure Anakinra Response Trial)
Author: Van Tassell BW, et al.
Comment: No formal between-group statistical test of all-cause mortality was reported (trial not powered for clinical events); only event counts/percentages are available. Deaths were all cardiac deaths per Supplemental Table 6 (Death = Cardiac Death in every arm), so all-cause = cardiac death counts here. Ns are final analysed Ns (18/16/18) rather than randomised (20/20/20); 8 patients were lost to follow-up before week 2.
Participant type: Adults (≥21 y) recently hospitalized with acute decompensated systolic heart failure (LVEF<50%) and CRP >2 mg/L, within 14 days of discharge
Recruitment source: Consecutive hospitalized patients screened at Virginia Commonwealth University, Richmond, VA
Outcome measurement: Number of deaths per randomized group, adjudicated by a dedicated clinical events committee
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality (death from any cause) at 24 weeks
additional_group_ns: Anakinra 2 wk: 1 death / n=16 (6%); Anakinra 12 wk: 0 deaths / n=18 (0%); both IL-1 blockade arms pooled into group_2 (1/34). Non-randomized observational no-treatment arm (n=50) had 6-month mortality 8% (4/50) and is excluded as it was not randomized.
effect_direction: favourable (1/34 with anakinra vs 1/18 with placebo; lower risk with anakinra)

Title: The effect of interleukin-1 receptor antagonist therapy on markers of inflammation in non-ST elevation acute coronary syndromes: the MRC-ILA Heart Study
Author: Morton et al.
Comment: Parenthetical values in Table 4 are incidence rates per 100 (per footnote), not percentages; event counts and randomised denominators (93 vs 89) used for the 2x2. The paper reports only a log-rank P-value for death, with no HR/RR estimate, so no ratio effect measure was recorded. Direction is more deaths in the IL-1ra arm.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('IL-1ra (Anakinra 100 mg s.c. daily for 14 days)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: cardiovascular medicine / anti-inflammatory therapy in acute coronary syndrome
Participant type: patients with non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (<48 h from chest pain onset, elevated troponin)
Recruitment source: five UK hospitals, cardiac and medical admission wards, July 2007 - March 2010
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with a death event over 1-year follow-up (incidence rate/100 in parentheses)
effect_direction: unfavourable (5/93 with anakinra vs 2/89 with placebo)

Title: Arterial Effects of Canakinumab in Patients With Atherosclerosis and Type 2 Diabetes or Glucose Intolerance
Author: Choudhury et al.
Comment: The paper reports no statistical test, risk ratio, or p value for death specifically; deaths are only tabulated as the main cause of study discontinuation. Zero events in the placebo arm.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Canakinumab 150 mg monthly') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: double-blind randomized placebo-controlled Phase II trial
Country: Canada, United Kingdom, United States, Germany, Israel
Participant type: Adults aged 18-74 with clinically evident atherosclerotic vascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus or impaired glucose tolerance
Recruitment source: 9 clinical trial centers (NCT00995930), randomization December 2009 to November 2012
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of randomised patients whose main cause of study discontinuation was death (Table 2)
effect_direction: unfavourable (1/95 with canakinumab vs 0/94 with placebo)

Title: Interleukin-1 Blockade Inhibits the Acute Inflammatory Response in Patients With ST-Segment–Elevation Myocardial Infarction (VCUART3)
Author: Abbate
Comment: Zero events in the anakinra arm; trial explicitly not powered for clinical outcomes. No RR/OR reported by the paper — only counts and a Fisher/chi-square P value.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Anakinra combined (100 mg once daily N=33 + twice daily N=31)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 2 trial
Participant type: Patients aged >=21 years presenting with acute ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing urgent coronary angiography within 12 h of symptom onset
Recruitment source: Virginia Commonwealth University Health, Virginia Cardiovascular Specialists, and Medstar Washington Hospital Center
Outcome measurement: Number (percentage) of patients who died, adjudicated by blinded independent committee
additional_group_ns: Anakinra once daily N=33 (0 deaths) and anakinra twice daily N=31 (0 deaths) were pooled into the combined anakinra arm (N=64) as reported by the paper's own 'Anakinra Combined' column; P value between the 3 groups = 0.40
effect_direction: favourable (0/64 with anakinra vs 1/35 with placebo)

Title: A randomised phase II study of interleukin-1 receptor antagonist in acute stroke patients
Author: Emsley HCA, Smith CJ, Georgiou RF, Vail A, Hopkins SJ, Rothwell NJ, Tyrrell PJ
Comment: Paper reports no risk ratio itself; only event counts, group event rates with 95% CIs, and p values (Fisher's exact p=1.0 for SAEs, p=0.65 for death rate, Kaplan-Meier log rank for survival). Deaths by 72 hours (1 active vs 3 placebo) are a subset of these 3-month counts and were not recorded separately to avoid double counting. Population is acute stroke rather than classic CVD secondary prevention.
Design Type: randomised, double blind, placebo controlled phase II trial
Participant type: patients within 6 hours of onset of acute stroke (ischaemic or primary intracerebral haemorrhage)
Recruitment source: acute teaching hospital trust (Salford Royal Hospitals NHS Trust), UK
Outcome measurement: Number of deaths per randomised group by 3 months
effect_direction: favourable (3/17 with rhIL-1ra vs 4/17 with placebo)

Report_ID: Death from any cause (all-cause mortality) — canakinumab all doses combined vs placebo
Title: Antiinflammatory Therapy with Canakinumab for Atherosclerotic Disease (CANTOS)
Author: Ridker et al.
Comment: Paper reports hazard ratios only (no risk ratio); event counts per arm are given and can be used to compute an RR downstream. Each dose arm shares the same placebo arm.
Participant type: Adults with previous myocardial infarction and hsCRP >=2 mg/L
Recruitment source: Central-laboratory screening at participating trial centers in 39 countries
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died from any cause / randomized per group; incidence rate per 100 person-years; stratified Cox hazard ratio
Outcome variable: Death from any cause (all-cause mortality) — canakinumab all doses combined vs placebo
additional_group_ns: Dose arms within the combined canakinumab group: 50 mg n=2170 (228 deaths); 150 mg n=2284 (238 deaths); 300 mg n=2263 (239 deaths)

Title: SCIL-STROKE (Subcutaneous Interleukin-1 Receptor Antagonist in Ischemic Stroke): A Randomized Controlled Phase 2 Trial
Author: Smith CJ, Hulme S, Vail A, Heal C, Parry-Jones AR, Scarth S, Hopkins K, Hoadley M, Allan SM, Rothwell NJ, Hopkins SJ, Tyrrell PJ
Comment: No verbatim per-group death counts are available in the extractable text: the paper only states narratively that "Mortality was similar between the allocation groups (Figure 1)", and the actual numbers of deaths appear solely inside the CONSORT diagram image, which is not reproduced as text. group_1_total/group_2_total are the randomized group sizes from the Baseline Characteristics table (IL-1Ra n=39; placebo n=41). Event counts left empty rather than invented, so no RR can be computed from this row as extracted.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Subcutaneous IL-1Ra (anakinra) 100 mg twice daily for 3 days (6 doses)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: adults within 5-6 hours of acute ischemic stroke onset (mean age 72 years, median NIHSS 12, 73% received IV alteplase)
Recruitment source: Greater Manchester Comprehensive Stroke Centre, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust
Outcome measurement: Deaths from any cause by 3-month follow-up, reported per randomized allocation group in the CONSORT diagram (Figure 1)
effect_direction: no clear difference reported ("mortality was similar between the allocation groups")
